articles.title: Are two readings as good as three for monthly linear accelerator output quality assurance?
articles.summary: This investigation assesses the efficacy of using two readings versus three for routine monthly output quality assurance on linear accelerators. The study concludes that two-reading protocols maintain consistent decision accuracy, providing a potential efficiency improvement for clinical physics workflows.

articles.title: A Dosimetric and Biological Comparison of Volumetric Modulated Arc Therapy and Adaptive Aperture Proton Therapy for Hippocampal-Sparing Whole-Brain Radiotherapy
articles.summary: This retrospective study compares the dosimetric outcomes of intensity-modulated proton therapy using Adaptive Aperture technology against VMAT for whole-brain radiotherapy. The findings demonstrate the potential for enhanced sparing of hippocampal structures and other organs at risk using the adaptive approach.

articles.title: Interpreting Dose LET volume histograms using difference mapping in Spot Delete proton planning
articles.summary: Researchers utilized difference mapping within Spot Delete proton planning to analyze biologically intensified dose distributions. The study concludes that this methodology effectively reduces elevated linear energy transfer to skin while maintaining consistent target dose coverage.

articles.title: Refining risk assessment in 177 Lu-DOTATATE extravasation: the value of 3D Monte Carlo dosimetry
articles.summary: This study evaluates the utility of 3D Monte Carlo dosimetry in assessing radiation risk following radiopharmaceutical extravasation. The results indicate that 3D modeling provides superior spatial insight into tissue dose distribution compared to standard MIRD methods.

articles.title: The Japanese Society for Radiation Oncology (JASTRO) guidelines on palliative radiotherapy for cancer-induced symptoms
articles.summary: The JASTRO guidelines for palliative radiotherapy have been updated following a systematic review of clinical evidence from 1970 to 2024. This document provides professional recommendations for managing cancer-induced symptoms through radiation intervention.

articles.title: Integrating functional brain regions into treatment optimization: a multi-institutional dosimetric study in CyberKnife SRT for brain metastases
articles.summary: This multi-institutional study explores the technical feasibility of incorporating functional neuroanatomical data into treatment planning for stereotactic radiosurgery. The authors report that this approach enables consistent dose reduction to critical brain regions without compromising target coverage.

articles.title: Off-axis Winston-Lutz quality assurance for static and rotational delivery on a gimbal-mounted O-ring linear accelerator
articles.summary: This paper evaluates the performance of a commercial Winston-Lutz procedure adapted for gimbal-shifted radiation therapy on an O-ring linear accelerator. The validation provides essential methodology for ensuring targeting accuracy during dynamic beam delivery.

articles.title: Multicenter Randomized Phase II Trial of Maintenance Systemic Therapy Versus Local Consolidative Therapy Plus Maintenance Systemic Therapy for Limited Metastatic Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NRG-LU002)
articles.summary: This phase II trial evaluated the impact of adding local consolidative therapy (LCT) to systemic maintenance therapy in oligometastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Results indicated that LCT did not improve progression-free or overall survival, suggesting that current patient selection criteria for LCT require further refinement.

articles.title: A patient-specific Winston-Lutz system for multi-target, single isocentre radiotherapy
articles.summary: This study introduces a quality assurance system designed to verify radiation targeting accuracy for multi-target, single-isocentre stereotactic radiosurgery. The system aims to ensure delivery precision for advanced radiotherapy techniques.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes After Pencil Beam Scanning Carbon Ion Radiotherapy for Unresectable Retroperitoneal Sarcomas
articles.summary: This exploratory analysis evaluates the safety and efficacy of pencil beam scanning carbon ion radiotherapy for unresectable retroperitoneal sarcomas. Findings suggest that higher linear energy transfer distribution within the target volume is associated with improved local control.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Proton and Conventional Radiation For Stage IIA and IIB Seminoma
articles.summary: This study reviews clinical outcomes for Stage IIA/IIB seminoma patients treated with radiation therapy. The authors note that modern techniques, including proton therapy, warrant further investigation to maintain high clinical efficacy while reducing long-term toxicities.

articles.title: Transforming Stereotactic Radiosurgery with Artificial Intelligence: Toward Intelligent Planning and Streamlined Workflows
articles.summary: As clinical indications for stereotactic radiosurgery expand, AI-driven solutions are becoming essential for managing complex, multi-lesion treatment plans. This review explores how machine learning can streamline workflows and improve planning efficiency.

articles.title: Toxicity risk in head and neck proton therapy: integrating physics, biology, and genomics
articles.summary: This research emphasizes the necessity of integrating physical dosimetric data with biological and genomic indicators to better predict and mitigate toxicity risks in head and neck proton therapy patients.

articles.title: Uncertainty-Aware Artificial Intelligence-Based Identification of Malignant Lymph Nodes on CT for a Prospective Trial of Involved Nodal Versus Elective Neck Radiotherapy
articles.summary: This study introduces a CT-based artificial intelligence model for identifying malignant lymph nodes in the neck. The model includes uncertainty estimation, which helps determine when clinician review is necessary, potentially enhancing clinical trial workflows.

articles.title: Systematic evaluation of energy window and reconstruction parameters for quantitative lutetium-177 SPECT imaging on a CZT-based starguide SPECT/CT system
articles.summary: This medical physics study establishes a standardized workflow for quantitative 177Lu SPECT imaging. The results support improved accuracy for personalized dosimetry in radiopharmaceutical therapy applications.

articles.title: Radiation-induced contrast enhancement in patients with IDH-mutated gliomas: incidence, risk factors, and impact of radiotherapy modality - a systematic review
articles.summary: This systematic review investigates the incidence and risk factors associated with radiation-induced contrast enhancement (RICE) in patients with IDH-mutated gliomas treated with proton therapy. The study addresses the clinical challenge of distinguishing RICE from tumor progression to improve patient management and outcomes.

articles.title: Paediatric radiotherapy in Denmark from 2008 to 2024: implementation of improved radiotherapeutic technologies
articles.summary: This nationwide study documents 16 years of technological advancements in pediatric radiotherapy implementation. The findings emphasize the role of clinical trials in driving the adoption of state-of-the-art conformal techniques for pediatric oncology.

articles.title: Advances in Radiotherapy for Glioblastoma and IDH-Mutant High-Grade Astrocytoma: A Biological and Mechanistic Perspective
articles.summary: This narrative review evaluates the current state of radiotherapy for high-grade gliomas, synthesizing biological and mechanistic data. It examines the reference standard of 60 Gy partial-brain regimens in the context of emerging molecular and clinical evidence.

articles.title: From Imaging Guidance to Dosimetric and Staging Superiority: Impact of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI on Target Delineation
articles.summary: This single-center retrospective study analyzes how the integration of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI influences target volume personalization and organs-at-risk sparing in prostate cancer radiotherapy. The results highlight the potential for improved staging and dosimetric precision with advanced imaging.

articles.title: Dose-painted VMAT for postoperative residual skull-base chordoma with 73.1 Gy residual-core escalation: A technical note
articles.summary: This study details the planning workflow and dosimetric profile of using VMAT to deliver high-dose escalation for residual skull-base chordoma. The report highlights the challenges of sparing the brainstem and optic apparatus while achieving therapeutic doses in complex anatomical regions.
